title: Fiber-Coherence CSP Equivalence
statement:
Let \(G\) have a stable vertex partition \(\mathcal P\), and let
\(K\subseteq\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}(G)\). For every type \(t\in V(K)\),
let \(F_t\) be the actual graph-edge fiber of type \(t\). For every
hyperedge \(h=\{t_1,t_2,t_3\}\), let
\[
C_h\subseteq F_{t_1}\times F_{t_2}\times F_{t_3}
\]
consist of the triples that form graph triangles. Then a
triangle-coherent section of \(K\) is exactly a satisfying assignment
of this constraint-satisfaction problem.

title: Coherence Factorization over Incidence Components
statement:
A fiber-coherence CSP admits a global section if and only if its
restriction to every connected component of its variable-constraint
incidence graph admits a section.

title: Star Support-Intersection Theorem
statement:
Suppose the hyperedges of \(K\) are \(h_i\) for \(i\in I\), all share
exactly one common type \(t\), and are otherwise pairwise disjoint.
Define
\[
S_i=\{e\in F_t:\text{ some tuple in }C_{h_i}\text{ uses }e\}.
\]
Then \(K\) admits a coherent section if and only if
\[
\bigcap_{i\in I}S_i\ne\varnothing.
\]

title: K4-Free Star-Support Universality
statement:
Let \(X\) be a set and let \(\{S_i:i\in I\}\) be nonempty subsets of
\(X\). There is a \(K_4\)-free graph with a stable partition whose
realized-type hypergraph is the star
\[
h_i=\{AB,AC_i,BC_i\},
\]
whose shared fiber \(F_{AB}\) is indexed by \(X\), and whose support
set at \(h_i\) is exactly \(S_i\).

title: Berge-Acyclic Coherence Frustration
statement:
There is a finite \(K_4\)-free graph and stable partition whose
realized-type hypergraph has two hyperedges sharing one type, so its
incidence graph is a tree, but the full type hypergraph has no coherent
section.

title: Arbitrarily Large Minimal Acyclic Frustration
statement:
For every integer \(n\ge2\), there is a finite \(K_4\)-free
star-shaped fiber-coherence system with exactly \(n\) constraints that
is unsatisfiable, while every proper constraint subsystem is
satisfiable.

title: No Bounded Local Coherence Test
statement:
For every finite \(m\), there is a finite \(K_4\)-free Berge-acyclic
fiber system such that every subsystem with at most \(m\) constraints
has a coherent section, while the full system does not.

title: Countable Compactness Failure with Infinite Fibers
statement:
There is a countable \(K_4\)-free star-shaped fiber system for which
every finite constraint subsystem has a coherent section but the full
system has none.

title: Finite-Fiber Coherence Compactness
statement:
Let \(K\) be any possibly infinite fiber-coherence CSP in which every
domain \(F_t\) is finite. If every finite constraint subsystem admits a
coherent section, then the whole system admits a coherent section.

title: Exact Fiber-Compactness Boundary
statement:
Finite edge fibers satisfy coherence compactness by CC09, whereas
countably infinite fibers do not, even for \(K_4\)-free star-shaped
systems whose type hypergraph is Berge-acyclic.

title: Regular-Cardinal Frustration Spectrum
statement:
For every infinite regular cardinal \(\lambda\), there is a
\(K_4\)-free star-shaped fiber system with \(\lambda\) constraints such
that every subsystem of cardinality less than \(\lambda\) has a
coherent section, while the full system has none.

title: Incidence-Tree Message Theorem
statement:
Let a finite fiber-coherence CSP have a variable-constraint incidence
graph that is a tree. For an oriented incidence edge define messages by
\[
M_{t\to h}=\bigcap_{g\in N(t)\setminus\{h\}}M_{g\to t},
\]
with the empty intersection equal to \(F_t\), and for
\(h=\{t,u,v\}\),
\[
M_{h\to t}=\{e_t\in F_t:\exists e_u\in M_{u\to h},e_v\in M_{v\to h}
\text{ with }(e_t,e_u,e_v)\in C_h\}.
\]
After inward message computation toward any root variable \(r\), the
CSP is satisfiable if and only if
\[
\bigcap_{h\in N(r)}M_{h\to r}\ne\varnothing.
\]

title: Star Theorem as Message-Passing Specialization
statement:
On a star-shaped type hypergraph, the incidence-tree message theorem
reduces exactly to the support-intersection criterion of CC03.

title: Polynomial-Time Acyclic Coherence
statement:
A finite fiber-coherence CSP with an acyclic incidence graph can be
decided, and a coherent section reconstructed when one exists, in time
polynomial in the explicitly listed domain and constraint-relation
sizes.

title: Minimal Frustration Core Certificate
statement:
Every finite incoherent fiber system contains an inclusion-minimal
incoherent constraint subsystem \(K\). For every constraint
\(h\in E(K)\), there is an assignment satisfying all constraints of
\(K-h\).

title: Cycle-or-Pruning Obstruction Dichotomy
statement:
Let a finite fiber-coherence CSP be incoherent. Then either its incidence
graph contains a cycle, or its incidence graph is a forest and the
message computation of CC12 produces an empty root intersection in one
component. In the latter case the emptied messages give an explicit
acyclic frustration certificate.

title: Finite-Fiber Exact-Compression Dichotomy
statement:
Let \(G\) have a stable partition \(\mathcal P\) whose nonempty edge
fibers are finite. Exactly one of the following holds:
1. some finite subhypergraph of \(\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}(G)\) has no
   triangle-coherent section;
2. the full realized-type hypergraph has a coherent section, and
   \[
   tc(G)=\chi(\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}(G)).
   \]
If \(G\) is \(K_4\)-free, outcome 2 also forces
\(\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}(G)\) to be Berge-\(C_3\)-free.

title: Unique-Fiber Exactness
statement:
If every nonempty part-pair fiber of a stable partition contains exactly
one graph edge, then the full realized-type hypergraph has a unique
coherent section and
\[
tc(G)=\chi(\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}(G)).
\]
After deleting isolated type vertices, the realized-type hypergraph is
naturally isomorphic to the triangle hypergraph of the triangle core
of \(G\).

title: Finite-Obstruction or Compressed #595 Witness
statement:
Let \(G\) be a hypothetical Erdős #595 witness and let \(\mathcal P\)
be any stable partition with finite edge fibers. Then either:
1. a finite realized-type subsystem is coherence-frustrated; or
2. \(\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}(G)\) is an uncountably chromatic,
   Berge-\(C_3\)-free, coherently sectioned 3-uniform hypergraph and
   \[
   tc(G)=\chi(\mathcal R_{\mathcal P}(G)).
   \]

title: Page-Free Finite-Fiber Close Dichotomy
statement:
In the page-free unary-homogeneous induced witness produced by HG21,
every stable partition with finite edge fibers has the same dichotomy as
CC19: a finite coherence-frustration certificate exists, or the entire
surviving obstruction is represented exactly by an uncountably
chromatic Berge-\(C_3\)-free coherently sectioned type hypergraph.

title: Finite Frustration-Number Spectrum
statement:
Define the frustration number of a finite fiber system as the minimum
number of constraints in an incoherent subsystem, with value infinity
when the full system is coherent. Among finite \(K_4\)-free star-shaped
systems, every value
\[
2,3,4,\dots,\infty
\]
occurs.

title: Acyclicity Gives Algorithms, Not Automatic Coherence
statement:
Berge acyclicity of the realized-type hypergraph does not imply
coherence, even in finite \(K_4\)-free systems. What acyclicity does
provide is an exact polynomial-time message criterion.

title: Two Orthogonal K4-Free Frustration Modes
statement:
The currently proved local frustration mechanisms in \(K_4\)-free
fiber systems are orthogonal:
1. **support frustration**, which already occurs on Berge-acyclic stars
   through empty support intersections;
2. **cycle coherence frustration**, where FC11 forbids a coherent
   Berge-\(C_3\).
Therefore any complete finite classification must track both domain
support propagation and cyclic endpoint compatibility.

title: Minimal Fiber-Coherence Classification Target
